The project

Applying for jobs creates a lot of disconnected work: researching a role, checking requirements, finding the right résumé, drafting answers, and remembering what was submitted. I built Career Agent to keep those pieces together in a workspace on the candidate’s own computer.

The React dashboard is the system of record. A user saves their profile and preferences once, then works with their own assistant to research opportunities and prepare applications. The candidate reviews the exact answers and documents before asking the assistant to submit an approved batch.

My role
Creator of the application and shared agent workflow
Format
Single-user local application; MIT licensed
Storage
SQLite by default; optional Supabase

From research to a reviewed application

Discover and assess

Public Greenhouse, Lever, and Ashby feeds bring in opportunities. Role fit, compensation, and sponsorship checks retain the evidence behind a decision.

Prepare with facts

Saved profile facts, reusable answers, document choices, and missing questions become a versioned review packet. Duplicate checks compare employer and role identities.

Review and record

The user reviews exact packets and authorizes submission separately. History distinguishes confirmed submissions, failures, uncertain results, and manual handoffs.

How it works

A typed domain engine sits between the interface, storage, and agent tools. It owns application state and approval rules; the assistant handles research and employer forms.

  1. Dashboard and API

    React presents profile, opportunities, review packets, and history. A loopback Express API validates requests.

  2. Domain engine

    Shared TypeScript contracts coordinate evidence, eligibility, packet versions, duplicate checks, and attempt transitions.

  3. Storage and agents

    SQLite transactions or Supabase revision checks persist state. A typed CLI connects the shared workflow to an assistant.

Original PDFs are preserved and verified with SHA-256. The public repository and this preview use fictional examples.

A key decision

An approval belongs to an exact version.

Changing application answers or documents invalidates an older approval. A prepared packet and a confirmed submission are separate states, and uncertain outcomes need reconciliation before a retry.

That separation is the core engineering choice: the assistant can do repetitive work while the candidate keeps control over what is sent. The dashboard does not launch an invisible background agent.
